task.goal: A webhook receiver uses SQLite to avoid processing the same event twice. It currently marks events done before the handler succeeds, so retries are lost; duplicate deliveries can also race. Fix process_event(db, event_id, payload, handler) in webhook.py. Return True only when this call handled the event, False for an already completed event. Roll back claims on handler failure, preserve a completed result across new connections, and avoid duplicate handler execution for sequential duplicate deliveries. Run tests and validate.

result.text:
I'll start by inspecting the workspace.Now the fix. The bug: the row is inserted with `done=1` before the handler runs, so a failing handler leaves a completed marker and retries return `False`; there is also no atomic claim, so two deliveries can both pass the `SELECT` and both run the handler.Fixed `process_event` in webhook.py: the row is now inserted as an unfinished claim (`done=0`) whose primary key is the serialization point, so exactly one delivery owns an event; `done=1` is only written after the handler returns. On handler failure the claim row is deleted and the exception re-raised, so retries still process the event. Completed rows are committed, so a new connection sees them.

Validation: `python3 -m unittest -v test_webhook` — 5/5 pass, covering duplicate suppression, retry after handler failure, durability across a new connection, sequential duplicates (handler runs once), and a two-thread concurrent delivery race (exactly one `True`, handler ran once).
